planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; set out into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after nights stay reliably above 55°F. Neon is compact and early-maturing, making it a good fit for containers as well as garden beds.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Neon produces smooth, glossy, vividly hot-pink to magenta fruit that stands out sharply against the plant's foliage, with mild, tender, nearly seedless flesh similar to standard Italian eggplants. It matures notably early for an eggplant and sets fruit heavily on a relatively compact plant, making it a productive choice for smaller gardens and containers as well as open beds. Harvest at 4-6 inches long while the skin is still glossy and firm, since fruit left too long dulls in color and toughens. Its striking coloring also makes it a popular market and specialty-produce variety.

common_name: Patio Baby Eggplant (AAS-Winning Compact Container Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; Patio Baby stays under two feet tall, making it well suited to containers, patios, and small raised beds where full-sized eggplants would not fit.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, or a large container with good drainage; Patio Baby is an All-America Selections winner bred specifically for compact, spineless, well-behaved growth that fits easily on a patio or in a small raised bed while still producing a heavy crop of glossy, deep-purple, egg-sized fruit. It bears notably early and continues producing over a long season, with tender, mild, nearly seedless flesh typical of good eating quality eggplant. Harvest fruit at 2-3 inches long while glossy and firm, and its small stature and prolific habit make it a favorite for container vegetable gardens with limited space.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; set out into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after nights stay reliably above 55°F, staking heavily loaded plants for support.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Prosperosa is a traditional Italian heirloom producing large, round to oval fruit in deep violet-purple with faint pale striping near the calyx, and dense, creamy, mild-flavored flesh well suited to grilling, roasting, and classic Italian preparations like eggplant parmesan. Plants are vigorous and productive, often needing staking to support the weight of the large fruit, and perform reliably through a long, hot growing season. Harvest while the skin is still glossy and firm and the fruit gives slightly to gentle pressure, since overripe fruit develops a bitter edge and coarser seeds.
